item.title: Codeberg Status (@codebergstatus@social.anoxinon.de)
item.description:
As you probably noticed, our domain codeberg.org is entirely unreachable.
It was registered with namesilo and entirely disappeared from our account. We're waiting for their customer support to investigate the situation.
No, we didn't forget to renew. There are no suspicious logins in the login history. There is no entry about the situation in the account's domain history.
We'll try setting up a workaround on our codeberg.eu domain ASAP.

item.title: I joined the NTP Pool, but not with my Stratum 1 Pi
item.description: Before I get too deep into the time-nuts rabbit hole, I figured I should share a little bit of the good time I now have in my studio, with everyone else. Thus, I've finally joined the NTP Pool, offering one public Stratum 2 NTP time server (ntp-01.jeffgeerling.com), which gets its time from my Stratum 1 time server (time.jeffgeerling.com) in the studio. My Time Pi is connected to an outside GNSS antenna through a TimeHAT v6, which I paired with a high quality timing-grade GNSS module, the u-blox ZED-F9T.

codeberg.org is unfortunately down right now due to a yet undefined issue with our domain. We are sorry for the inconveniences & are working on a solution.

item.title: Google's AI Overviews cut clicks to websites by 40%
item.description: Google's AI answers are taking clicks from websites in the search results. In a randomized experiment, researchers hid AI Overviews from some US desktop users. Comparing them with users who still saw Overviews shows that an Overview cuts clicks to outside websites by about 40%. Those Overviews now appear on more than half the US keywords DataForSEO tracks, up from 6% two years ago. The industry's answer, GEO (generative engine optimization), has yet to show a way to compensate for the loss. While AI citations correlate with the same kind of link profile that goes with higher Google rankings, in March AI assistants sent websites just 0.3% of their traffic.
